title: BaseHTTPMiddleware lifecycle candidate boundary audit

boundary_decision.rationale: Issue 2516 explicitly cites PR 1715 as a supposed prior fix, but the earlier segment concerns background-task completion and cancellation tradeoffs while the later segment has a distinct client-disconnect race, multi-middleware reproducer, rejected patch, and final non-polling fix. The citation is a historical dependency, not proof of one root cause.
boundary_decision.falsification: Recombine only if an immutable patch/test analysis demonstrates one causal defect whose state transitions account for both the original background-task behavior and the later No-response race without relying on the citation alone.

excluded_sources.reason: The create_task workaround is not a verified fix and later discussion distinguishes blocking CPU work from the middleware defect.
The abandoned response-evaluation direction is summarized by the included maintainer analysis; expanding it would create a separate branch.
Pure ASGI middleware is a valid workaround but does not explain or resolve the later race in BaseHTTPMiddleware.
A 2025 SSE reproduction occurs after the registered merge outcome and does not establish that it is the same race; it is preserved as an Outcome limitation instead of being back-propagated.

source_body_history_limitations: The current PR bodies are mutable snapshots. Segment membership relies on timestamped comments, conservative summaries, and immutable merge anchors; no summary treats the later citation as proof of identical root cause.
